question: How much residual moisture did the water-processed NMC532 cathode lose between 20 °C and drying at 120 °C, and how does its final value compare with the NMP-processed cathode dried at 100 °C?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM atoms WHERE lower(text) LIKE '%moisture%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%water content%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%ppm%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%120%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%dried%' OR lower(text) LIKE '%drying%' ORDER BY page, id
SELECT id, page, text FROM atoms WHERE id IN ('p8.L50','p8.L51','p8.L52','p8.L53','p8.L54','p8.L55','p8.L56','p8.L57','p8.L58','p8.L59','p8.L60','p9.L1','p9.L2') ORDER BY id

WITH v AS (
SELECT CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L54'),'and (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) AS wet_start,
CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L59'),'and (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) AS wet_final,
CAST(regexp_extract((SELECT text FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L56'),'reduced to (\d+) ppm',1) AS INTEGER) AS nmp_final)
SELECT wet_start - wet_final AS water_loss, wet_final - nmp_final AS water_minus_nmp, wet_final, nmp_final, wet_start FROM v

rendered: The water-processed NMC532 cathode started at 625 ppm of residual moisture at 20[1] and ended at 47 ppm[2] after drying at a higher temperature of 110-120[3] °C. The moisture it lost was 578[4] ppm. The NMP-processed cathode, by contrast, reduced to 87 ppm after drying at 100[5] °C under vacuum. So the water-processed cathode's final value is lower than the NMP-processed value, by 40[6] ppm. For reference, the water-based cathode dried under the same vacuum conditions as the NMP cathode retained 160 ppm[7], so it needed the higher drying temperature to fall below the NMP value.
